label: Host skeptical + red-bar brain (face-led, 'WHY PLAY?')
prompt: A photorealistic 16:9 YouTube thumbnail, cinematic and premium. A thoughtful man in his early 30s, short dark hair, light stubble, wearing a plain off-white crew-neck shirt, framed chest-up and positioned on the LEFT third of the frame, against a seamless dark charcoal #323232 studio background. A single hard key light from the left and a subtle rim light separate him from the background, which is very slightly darker and softly blurred. His expression is GENUINE SKEPTICAL CURIOSITY: brows slightly knit, one eyebrow marginally raised, mouth closed, direct intense eye contact with the camera. He is NOT shocked, NOT smiling, NOT open-mouthed. In the upper-right area floats a clean minimalist icon of a side-view human brain constructed from thin vertical bars in off-white #f8f8f8, with the single central vertical bar glowing bright red #309420. That red is the ONLY saturated colour anywhere in the image. In the upper-left, bold condensed sans-serif text reads exactly "WHY PLAY?" in off-white #f8f8f8. High contrast, lots of negative space, rigorous and intelligent mood. The ONLY text in the entire image is "WHY PLAY?". Keep the bottom-right corner clear. Text must be crisp, bold and perfectly legible even at small size.

label: Before/after split brain: deleted vs alive (pure concept)
prompt: A minimalist conceptual 16:9 YouTube thumbnail, split into two equal vertical panels divided by a thin off-white #f8f8f8 seam, both panels on a dark charcoal #323232 background. LEFT panel: a side-view human brain icon made of thin vertical bars, rendered entirely in dull desaturated grey-white, dim, faded and visibly incomplete, with NO colour. RIGHT panel: the same brain icon in crisp off-white #f8f8f8 vertical bars, but its single central bar blazes bright red #309420 and extends beyond the brain outline, with a few thin off-white neuron-like lines branching energetically off it, so the brain looks fully alive and electrified. The image reads instantly as 'remove the red and the brain is dim and incomplete; keep the red and it comes alive.' The ONLY saturated red is in the right panel, pulling the eye there. One small bold off-white word "DELETE?" sits low in the LEFT panel. The ONLY text in the image is "DELETE?". Extremely high contrast, premium, restrained, mobile-legible. Keep the bottom-right corner clear.
